_readme: T2.9 golden set. Every `expected` block carries `reviewed_by`, which says
whose judgement it is. Three values:
deterministic    -- the verdict follows from arithmetic in `synthesis.py`
(integrity floor, coverage ratio) and no judgement of
mine is in it. Zero circularity.
assistant-draft  -- scored by Claude against the published rubric, at the
owner's explicit instruction. Better than unreviewed,
weaker than a human analyst. An eval report MUST say so
rather than printing the result as plain accuracy.
human            -- an analyst read the profile and decided. None yet.
Money is integer minor units (kobo for NGN, cents for USD), per CLAUDE.md
section 6. Figures inside each company are internally consistent on purpose:
`consistency.check_scale` fires at a 10x discrepancy, so an unintended
mismatch would flag a finding the expectations do not predict. Company
`unit-error-kobo` breaks that deliberately and says so.
`data_integrity_min` and `data_integrity_max` are EQUAL everywhere. That
score is arithmetic over a fixed penalty table, so a band would be slack
hiding a wrong answer -- the exact figure is derivable and is asserted.
`saleability_below_fundability` is optional and set on one company. It says
the fixture's claim is the GAP between the two verdicts rather than either
band on its own, and the accuracy half must compare the observed scores
directly -- two bands, however tight, are both satisfied by a run that
scored the two verdicts the same.
`verdict_is_model_dependent` marks companies whose verdict cannot be
predicted without a real model call: the dimension scores come from
claude-opus-5. Where it is false, the verdict is decided by arithmetic
alone and the deterministic layer can assert it with no API call.
THREE STRUCTURAL FACTS THE SCORING PASS UNCOVERED. Read these before
trusting any band below; all three are recorded in TASKS.md T2.9.
1. Score bands assume the UNWEIGHTED floor mean that `_verdict_for`
actually computes. `DimensionSpec.weight` is defined on all 11
dimensions, its docstring claims 'Synthesis (T2.7) applies these', and
nothing reads it. Applying the weights would move every band here.
2. `ready` and `not_yet` both require EVERY in-scope dimension to come back
`sufficient` -- `thin = unevidenced or any(PROVISIONAL)` in
`_verdict_for`. One hedged dimension out of ten collapses the whole
verdict to `provisional`. That makes the four non-provisional
expectations below the most fragile assertions in this file.
3. `market_opportunity` and `scalability` had NO field behind them until
2026-08-03 -- their substance was hand-written into `description` and
`business_model`, and this file carried a length proxy to decide whether
enough had been written. `market_size_note`, `competition_note`,
`growth_constraint` and `use_of_funds` replaced that workaround, and the
fixtures below now answer the real questions. One criterion is still
unserved: scalability wants the marginal-cost-per-customer trend, which
nothing asks for. See FOUNDER-ONBOARDING.md.
`healthy-seed-fintech` expecting `ready` is still a claim about what
SHOULD happen rather than a prediction. The benchmark table is empty, so
every dimension is scored with the model told to lower its confidence --
and per fact 2 one hedged dimension is enough to collapse the verdict.

companies.why_this_case: The unambiguous pass, and the only fixture that asserts `ready`. If this does not come out ready on fundability, either the bar is wrong, the rubric is broken, or -- most likely on the first run -- some dimension came back hedged because no benchmark band matched and the prompt tells the model to lower its confidence when none does. Check that before touching READY_THRESHOLD. Every dimension is answered from a real field, including the market derivation (12,000 Lagos outlets x NGN 5,000, reconciling with the stated monthly revenue) and the named growth constraint, so a `provisional` result here is about scoring rather than about missing data.

description.value: Payment collection for Lagos pharmacies, settling same-day.

business_model.value: 1.2% per transaction plus a monthly SaaS fee of NGN 5,000 per outlet. An outlet costs nothing further to serve once it is live, so gross margin rises with every cohort.

key_person_dependency.value: Nothing critical. Both founders can cover sales and ops, and the settlement integration is documented and run by two engineers. We hold a CBN mobile money operator licence in the company name, not personally.

cap_table_summary.value: The two founders hold 78% between them, a 2022 pre-seed angel round holds 12%, and 10% sits in an employee option pool. No debt and no convertible instruments outstanding. All engineering IP is assigned to the company by written agreement, including the two contractors used in 2023.

market_size_note.value: Lagos State has roughly 12,000 registered pharmacy outlets. At our NGN 5,000 average monthly fee that is a serviceable market of about NGN 60m a month, and we hold 900 of those outlets. We cannot address the rest of Nigeria yet: each state needs its own pharmacy council registration, so the figure is deliberately Lagos-only rather than a national headline.

competition_note.value: Cash reconciliation done by hand, which is what most outlets still do, and the general-purpose POS terminals from Moniepoint and OPay. Neither competitor reconciles a payment back to the pharmacy's stock ledger, which is the specific thing our customers stay for.

growth_constraint.value: Field onboarding, not technology. One field agent signs about 40 outlets a month and we run three agents. An outlet costs nothing further to serve once live, so the constraint is purely how fast we can sign them. We have already run this motion twice inside Lagos and can evidence the per-agent numbers.

use_of_funds.value: Field agents and the state-by-state pharmacy council registrations that open the next market. Roughly 70% headcount for agents, 30% registration and compliance. Both map directly to the onboarding constraint rather than to product work.

companies.why_this_case: Enough evidence to judge, and it does not meet the bar. Guards against a rubric that never says not_yet -- which is why it is enriched rather than left thin: a thin profile can only ever produce `provisional`, so an unenriched fixture would guard nothing. Two months of runway, LTV/CAC of 1.4, and one of three founders working full time.

description.value: On-demand errand running for Abuja households.

business_model.value: Flat fee per errand, averaging NGN 5,000 a household a month.

key_person_dependency.value: The one full-time founder does dispatch, support and collections personally. Nothing runs for more than a day without him.

cap_table_summary.value: Three founders hold the company equally at 33.3% each. No outside investment, no option pool, and no written IP assignment from the contractor who built the dispatch app.

market_size_note.value: We estimate 180,000 Abuja households can afford a paid errand service, which at our NGN 5,000 monthly average is about NGN 900m a month; we hold 30 of them. This is our own estimate derived from national household income bands, not a published market study, and should be treated as soft.

competition_note.value: The informal okada rider a household already uses and knows, which is our real competition, and increasingly Chowdeck and Glovo. Both of those are far better capitalised than we are.

growth_constraint.value: Rider supply in the neighbourhoods we cover. Cost per errand has not fallen as we have grown -- at 30 households we pay the same per-trip rate we paid at 10, because riders are paid per job and no neighbourhood yet has the density to batch trips.

use_of_funds.value: Rider guarantees, to hold a pool long enough for density to build. We have never demonstrated that a guaranteed pool holds retention, so this is funding an attempt rather than scaling a proven motion, and we would say so to an investor.

companies.why_this_case: CLAUDE.md section 5's hard rule: thin data yields insufficient_data, never a confident answer. The failure this guards is a false 'not fundable' for someone who was simply never assessed. No dimension has any citable evidence, so coverage is 0 and the verdict is decided before any model call.

description.value: Something in agriculture. Still working it out.

companies.why_this_case: Whole naira typed into a kobo field, by a founder who also miscounted the team. Integrity must fall below the floor (50) and BOTH verdicts must be withheld without the rubric ever being called -- the pipeline skips the most expensive call in the platform when the verdict is already decided. Note it takes three findings to get there: two LIKELY at 15 each only reach 70, so a fixture meant to breach the floor needs a CERTAIN in it. The first draft of this company did not, and the determinism suite caught it. 100 - 15 - 15 - 25 = 45.

description.value: Grain aggregation and resale to processors.

business_model.value: Buy at farmgate, sell to mills.

companies.why_this_case: Revenue is absent, not zero. finance.py returns None-plus-a-reason rather than 0.0 precisely so this does not get scored as a real 0% margin, which would be the false verdict section 5 forbids. Also the fixture that keeps market opportunity and scalability independent: it answers the market questions honestly (a real derivation, bounded by the certification it has not got) and leaves the growth questions empty, because a pre-clinical company genuinely cannot evidence that capital would produce output. Fundability lands at 5/8 rather than 4/8 as a result -- and 4/8 is exactly the `covered < 0.5` boundary, where a single field would swing the whole verdict between provisional and insufficient_data.

business_model.value: Per-unit sales to clinics once certified.

key_person_dependency.value: The chief scientist holds the assay formulation. There is no second person who could complete certification.

market_size_note.value: Nigeria records around 60 million malaria cases a year, and the National Malaria Elimination Programme puts rapid-test consumption near 30 million units annually. At our target price of NGN 250 a strip that is roughly NGN 7.5bn a year. We can address none of it until NAFDAC certification completes, so the market we can actually serve today is zero.

competition_note.value: Imported SD Bioline and Abbott rapid tests, which is what clinics buy now. We expect to undercut them on landed cost rather than beat them on sensitivity.

companies.why_this_case: The two verdicts must be able to diverge. A profitable agency that dies without its founder is fundable-ish and clearly less saleable; if both verdicts always move together, the saleability dimensions are not doing any work. Note how little they can currently diverge: 7 of the 10 saleability dimensions are shared with fundability, and because the unweighted mean ignores `DimensionSpec.weight`, the three saleability-only dimensions carry 30% of the verdict instead of the 50% the declared weights give them. The gap below is roughly 10 points; under the declared weights it would be about twice that. The ordering is the claim and the bands are only its shadow, so this is the one fixture carrying `saleability_below_fundability`: the accuracy half must compare the two observed scores directly, not just check each against its band. The bands are also deliberately made not to overlap (46-69 against 32-45), because two overlapping bands are both satisfied by a run that scored the verdicts identically -- which is the exact failure this company exists to catch.

description.value: Brand campaigns for consumer goods, sold personally by the founder.

business_model.value: Project retainers, averaging NGN 200,000 a client a month.

key_person_dependency.value: Every client was won personally by the founder and renews on that relationship. There is no account manager and no written pipeline.

cap_table_summary.value: The founder holds 100%. No outside investors, no option pool, no debt. Campaign creative is delivered under client contracts that assign copyright to the client, so the agency owns no reusable IP.

market_size_note.value: About 400 consumer-goods companies in Nigeria run paid brand campaigns of the size we service. At our NGN 200,000 monthly average that is a serviceable market near NGN 80m a month, of which we hold 14 accounts. The count comes from the industry association's member list rather than a purchased report.

competition_note.value: The Lagos offices of the network agencies for the largest accounts, and freelancers below us on price. We win on the founder's personal relationships rather than on price or on any proprietary method, which is the honest answer.

growth_constraint.value: Senior creative hours, which scale linearly with headcount. Delivery cost per additional client has been flat for three years at roughly 40% of that client's fee, and we hold no template, product, or reusable method that would bend it.

use_of_funds.value: More senior creatives. Capital buys people, not leverage -- every naira of new revenue needs about the same share of a senior creative as the last one did, so this would fund a larger version of the same shape rather than a different one.

companies.why_this_case: Sits deliberately near READY_THRESHOLD (70, currently untuned). Hand-scoring puts it at about 68 on fundability, which is the point: this is the company whose verdict should move when the threshold is tuned. Treat a score of 70 or above here as a signal to look at the threshold, NOT automatically as a regression -- the band below stops just under 70 so the level assertion stays meaningful, but an eval report should surface this company's raw score every run rather than only its pass or fail.

description.value: Inter-city parcel delivery across northern Nigeria.

business_model.value: Per-parcel pricing by weight and distance, averaging NGN 5,000 a month an account.

key_person_dependency.value: Routes and pricing are documented and the ops lead runs them day to day. The founders are replaceable within a quarter.

cap_table_summary.value: Two founders hold 70%, a 2021 friends-and-family round holds 20%, and 10% is an unallocated option pool. No debt. The dispatch software is a licensed third-party product, not owned, which is why ip_owned is false.

market_size_note.value: The eight northern states we cover generate roughly 90,000 inter-city commercial parcels a month at the weights we carry, which at our NGN 5,000 average is a serviceable market of about NGN 450m a month. Derived from state trade-association parcel counts rather than a purchased market report.

competition_note.value: GIG Logistics on the trunk routes, and the informal luxury-bus parcel trade everywhere else. The second is much larger than the first and is what we actually take share from.

growth_constraint.value: Depot coverage. Each new depot opens a route cluster and costs about NGN 18m to stand up, after which marginal cost per parcel on that cluster falls with volume. We have run this four times and can evidence the unit cost.

use_of_funds.value: Depots, at roughly NGN 18m each, plus the vehicles to serve each new cluster. This maps directly to the coverage constraint and is a motion we have already run four times.

companies.why_this_case: Arithmetically impossible rather than merely improbable: more founders than people. A CERTAIN-severity finding, so it must fire regardless of how forgiving the thresholds are. 100 - 25 = 75, which is above the integrity floor, so unlike unit-error-kobo the rubric IS called and the finding has to survive into a real verdict rather than short-circuiting it. Left deliberately thin -- the claim here is about the finding, not about the score, and enriching it would only add noise to a fixture whose job is one CERTAIN check.

description.value: Custom internal tooling for mid-sized manufacturers.
